name: The Strip and Paradise
tagline: Resort corridor of casinos, shows and high-rise condos
description: The four mile stretch of Las Vegas Boulevard lined with mega-resorts, plus the condo towers just behind it in Paradise. Short-term rentals in buildings like Turnberry and Panorama put pools, gyms and restaurants downstairs. Convenient for visitors, exhausting as a long-term home.
bestFor: Short-stay nomads in town for conferences who want everything on foot.
pros: Walk to hundreds of restaurants and venues
Monorail and airport are both close
Condo towers include gyms and pools
cons: Constant crowds and noise, day and night
Groceries and everyday errands are awkward

name: Downtown and the Arts District
tagline: Fremont Street plus the city's creative warehouse quarter
description: Old Vegas around Fremont Street, and just south of it the 18b Arts District, where warehouses now hold breweries, vintage shops, coffee roasters and murals. This is the closest the city has to a walkable independent neighbourhood, and most of its coworking and cafe scene lives here.
bestFor: Nomads who want independent cafes, bars and a real neighbourhood over resort life.
pros: Genuinely walkable core with monthly art walks
cons: Visible homelessness and rough blocks nearby
Some streets feel unsafe walking late
Fremont Street itself gets loud and messy

name: Chinatown on Spring Mountain Road
tagline: A two mile corridor of the city's best cheap food
description: Strip malls along Spring Mountain Road holding hundreds of Chinese, Korean, Japanese, Vietnamese and Thai restaurants, plus 99 Ranch and Asian bakeries. Apartment complexes just off the road rent well below Strip prices, and the Strip itself is a short drive east.
bestFor: Value-minded nomads who care more about food and rent than views.
pros: Outstanding cheap food, open very late
cons: Strip-mall layout, not pleasant to walk
Traffic on Spring Mountain is heavy at peak

name: Summerlin
tagline: Master-planned suburb against the Red Rock foothills
description: A large planned community on the western edge with tidy parks, trail networks, Downtown Summerlin's shops and quick access to Red Rock Canyon hiking. Rentals are newer, quieter and family oriented. It is the pick for anyone treating Vegas as a base rather than a party.
bestFor: Long-stay nomads and families who want quiet, trails and modern rentals.
pros: Red Rock hiking and bike trails minutes away
Newer homes with good internet options
cons: Twenty to thirty minutes from the Strip

name: Henderson and Green Valley
tagline: A separate, calmer city on the southeast side
description: Its own municipality bordering Las Vegas, built around the Green Valley area with strip parks, good schools, the District shopping centre and the trail out to Lake Mead. Crime rates are lower than the Vegas average and rentals skew toward newer townhouses and single-family homes.
bestFor: Remote workers staying several months who want suburban calm and safety.
pros: Among the safest areas in the valley
Plenty of parks and paved trails
cons: Longest commute to the Strip and airport
Very little nightlife or walkable street life
